requirements.evidence: All contract pieces are present: migrations with cascading FKs, unique (queue_id, code) and the recommended index (create_tickets_table.php:16-28); Queue model with fillable/casts/relations (app/Models/Queue.php:12-38); Entity::queues() (app/Models/Entity.php:46-49); enums; InactiveQueueException extends RuntimeException; IssueTicket checks for negative priority, locks and re-reads the queue inside a transaction, and retries on UniqueConstraintViolationException up to 5 times (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:24-55); nextCode walks rows by id desc and skips malformed codes (app/Models/Ticket.php:81-93); write-once updating hook (Ticket.php:35-45); call() checks membership and re-reads the status under a row lock (Ticket.php:101-123); the factory store() override allocates codes per ticket and keeps explicit codes (TicketFactory.php:46-53). Gap: because nextCode derives the number from the last remaining row, deleting the newest ticket (A003 out of A001..A003) makes the next code A003 again. The task says a deleted ticket's number is not reused, and the docs narrow this to 'when a later ticket exists' (docs/business-rules.md:525).

conventions.evidence: The domain write is an invokable Action (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php). Fillable is set deliberately (#[Fillable] on Queue.php:12 and Ticket.php:205). Migrations have reversible down() and generator-style timestamps. docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG [Unreleased] are updated, and public methods have PHPDoc. Deviation: Ticket::call() authorizes with an inline `$user->membershipFor($entityId)` check (Ticket.php:104-106) and not through a policy/gate, although conventions say authorization always goes through app/Policies.

security.evidence: call() refuses non-members with AuthorizationException before any write (Ticket.php:104-106), and the test confirms the ticket is unchanged (TicketModelTest.php:882-892). Inactive-queue state is read under lockForUpdate (IssueTicket.php:52). Mass assignment is controlled with Fillable. The write-once guard prevents tampering with code/priority through Eloquent. No HTTP surface in scope. Small gap: authorization logic sits in the model and is not reusable through a policy.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/Queue/IssueTicketTest.php covers defaults, sequential codes, negative priority, an inactive queue, a stale model deactivated in the DB, retry after a simulated collision and giving up after repeated collisions. TicketModelTest.php covers factory defaults, forQueue A001/A002, explicit 'A-X', count(3), per-queue uniqueness, A999->A1000->A1001, deleted middle ticket -> A004, both malformed-code cases, queue scoping, a write-once dataset over 5 fields via save() and update(), a single call, a double call, a stale instance call, a non-member call, cascade/nullOnDelete, and enum values. No test exists for deleting the last ticket, which is the case that would expose the reuse gap.

simplicity.evidence: Lean code: nextCode is a short lazyByIdDesc loop (Ticket.php:81-93), write-once is a single updating hook with a MUTABLE list, the retry is a plain for loop, and the factory needs only a 7-line store() override. No service or repository layers and no speculative abstractions.

readability.evidence: Clear names (MUTABLE, MAX_ATTEMPTS, forQueue, inactive), short focused methods, helpful comments ('Lock + re-read: the passed model may be stale.'), PHPDoc with @throws, and consistent sibling style (casts() method, @use HasFactory docblocks). No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: the models, enums, exception, action, factories, two migrations, tests and the doc/changelog updates the task requests. No HTTP, Livewire or call-next selection was added. The extra QueueFactory::inactive() state is used by the tests.

issues.explanation: nextCode derives the next number from the newest remaining valid row, so deleting the most recent ticket (A003 out of A001..A003) makes the next code A003 again, against the rule that a deleted ticket's number is not reused.
Call authorization is an inline membershipFor() check inside the model; conventions require authorization to go through policies/gates in app/Policies.
The docs narrow the no-reuse rule to 'when a later ticket exists', which records the gap above instead of fixing it.
The deletion test only covers a middle ticket; deleting the latest ticket is untested and would expose the number reuse.

review.summary: The change adds queues and tickets end to end: migrations, models with write-once and single-call enforcement, enums, factories with per-ticket code allocation, and an IssueTicket action that re-reads the queue under a lock and retries on code collisions, all with thorough Pest tests and updated docs. It is approvable with small fixes: deleting the newest ticket lets its number be reused, and call authorization uses an inline membership check instead of a policy. Confidence is medium because User::membershipFor and the sibling files are not in the diff.
